variants.headline: Looking back: building job cancelled part-way
variants.sub: The client has abandoned {project}, which {builder} was building.
variants.body:
We return to our earlier coverage. Our report recorded this: The building job for {project}, undertaken by {builder}, had been cancelled part-way.

A part-completed cancellation is a contract event, not a completed asset. Managers should distinguish the client's decision to abandon the plan from an assumed settlement of every obligation. Commercial scrutiny requires actual terms for financial consequences, rather than an automatic conclusion that the end of the job clears the account.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We fault {target} for inadequate stewardship. An undertaking abandoned part-way deserves serious scrutiny, and changing the plan should not be a convenient means of making responsibility for unfinished work disappear.

variants.headline: Looking back: client abandons the construction plan
variants.sub: Construction of {project} by {builder} has been cancelled before completion.
variants.body:

Commercial scrutiny requires actual terms for financial consequences, rather than an automatic conclusion that the end of the job clears the account.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.
